subject: astro-ph.CO
title_original: The MeerKAT Thousand-Pulsar Polarisation Array II: Searches for Ultralight Axion-Like Dark Matter
authors: Zi-Yan Yuwen, Michael Sarkis, Yin-Zhe Ma, Tao Liu, Jing Ren, Patrick Weltevrede, Xiao Xue
abstract: We construct Pulsar Polarisation Arrays (PPA), using regular pulsars monitored in MeerKAT's Thousand Pulsar Array (TPA) Programme, to search for Axion-like Dark Matter (ALDM) within Milky Way. Specifically, from a catalogue of 1237 regular pulsars, we select the 50 ones with the highest signal-to-noise ratio and set upper limits on the ALDM Chern-Simons coupling. We find no signals with statistical significance over the mass range of $[10^{-23},10^{-20}]\,{\rm eV}$ in the six-year MeerKAT's data. By combining the high-quality TPA pulsars and the accurate ionospheric subtraction of spinifex, we establish the most sensitive upper limits to the date on the ALDM Chern-Simons coupling, namely $\lesssim 10^{-14} - 3\times 10^{-13}\,{\rm GeV}^{-1}$, for the mass range of $[10^{-23},10^{-21}]\,{\rm eV}$ except at $m_a \sim 1.3 \times 10^{-22}\,$eV. This study underscores the great potential of constructing regular-pulsar PPAs for scientific tasks.
title_relatable: Can pulsars detect ultralight dark matter particles?
hook: Using 50 of MeerKAT's brightest pulsars, researchers set the tightest limits yet on a hypothetical dark matter candidate across six years of data.
summary: Astronomers built a pulsar polarization array from MeerKAT radio telescope observations to hunt for axion-like dark matter particles in the Milky Way. Analyzing polarization patterns from the 50 best-quality pulsars over six years revealed no signatures of this dark matter in the mass range 10^−23 to 10^−20 electronvolts, but they pinned down more restrictive constraints on how these particles would interact with light than any previous study.
